skill.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
skill.description: Guides migration of TypeScript test fixtures from `as` assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn helpers for partial or intentionally invalid test data.
skill.summary: Migrate TypeScript test fixtures from unsafe assertions to shoehorn helpers.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks and TypeScript examples, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. Two findings are confirmed because the skill instructs dependency installation with npm, which can modify project files and run package lifecycle scripts. I found no prompt injection or malicious data-exfiltration intent in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation is requested without explicit safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user for confirmation before installing, use the project package manager, preserve lockfiles, and consider pinning the shoehorn version.

content.value_statement: Type assertions in tests can hide missing fields and unclear intent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to replace them with shoehorn helpers.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use fromPartial, fromAny, and fromExact in tests.
Guides replacement of `as Type` with `fromPartial()` for partial test data.
Guides replacement of `as unknown as Type` with `fromAny()` for intentionally invalid data.
Recommends searching test and spec files, then running type checks.
limitations: Intended for test files only, not production code.
Requires project acceptance of @total-typescript/shoehorn as a dependency.
Does not automate a full repository migration by itself.
Needs human review for intentionally invalid test data.

use_cases.title: Clean Up TypeScript Tests
use_cases.description: Replace unsafe test assertions with shoehorn helpers while keeping the same test behavior.

use_cases.title: Simplify Large Test Fixtures
use_cases.description: Pass only the fields a test needs instead of building large fake objects.

use_cases.title: Guide Reviewable Migrations
use_cases.description: Create a clear migration plan that separates partial fixtures from intentionally invalid data.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate One Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner migration for a single file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this test file from TypeScript `as` assertions to shoehorn. Keep behavior unchanged and explain each replacement.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Test Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Find test and spec files with `as` assertions and propose a shoehorn migration plan before editing. Do not change production files.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Fixture Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration across several fixture styles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor partial test fixtures to use `fromPartial`, intentionally invalid fixtures to use `fromAny`, and full fixtures to use `fromExact`. Add imports and run type checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Assertion Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this test suite for unsafe type assertions, separate safe cases from intentional invalid data, migrate selected cases, and summarize remaining risks.

output_examples.input: A test builds a large request object only to supply one body field.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a partial helper, a package import, and a type check after the migration.

output_examples.input: A test passes invalid data on purpose to verify error handling.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the case as intentional invalid data and recommends the helper designed for that purpose.

output_examples.input: A team wants a safe migration plan for many test files.
output_examples.output: The skill separates discovery, dependency confirmation, focused edits, and final verification into reviewable steps.

best_practices: Use the skill only on test and spec files.
Confirm dependency changes before running install commands.
Run type checks and tests after each migration.
anti_patterns: Applying shoehorn helpers to production code.
Replacing assertions without understanding intentionally invalid data.
Skipping review of generated imports and dependency changes.

faq.question: What does this skill migrate?
faq.answer: It migrates TypeScript test assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn helpers for partial or intentionally invalid test data.

faq.question: Can I use it in production code?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that shoehorn should be used only in test code.

faq.question: Does it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends installing @total-typescript/shoehorn when needed. Confirm dependency changes before running install commands.

faq.question: Which helpers does it explain?
faq.answer: It explains fromPartial for partial data, fromAny for intentionally wrong data, and fromExact for full objects.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I check after migration?
faq.answer: Review changed tests, verify imports, run the type checker, and run the relevant test suite.
